title: Reset Before the Final Scan
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, let $\mathrm{orc}$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four indices and each finite Boolean word, and let $M\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory marking. For every machine state $S$ whose 17 register values are each at most $B$, there is a finite run from the reset stage before the final scan, with registers given by $S$, memory $M$, and memory head at $0$, to the final-scan preparation stage, with the registers $U,V,w,K,B_s$ set to zero, all other registers unchanged, memory still $M$, and head still at $0$. At every time strictly before the endpoint, the register and instruction safety conditions hold, and the memory head lies between $0$ and $P$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: Every register value in the machine state S is at most B
replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let an oracle assign Boolean answers to each of four
indices and each Boolean word, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $M:\mathbb
Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory marking. For every machine state $S$
whose registers are all at most $B$, the machine reaches, in finitely many steps, the
final-scan preparation state with the same memory marking and head at $0$, and with
$U,V,w,K,B_s$ reset to zero while all other registers retain their values from $S$. At
every time strictly before arrival, all registers are at most $B$, the current
instruction's required safety condition holds, and the memory head lies between $0$ and
$P$.
